title: Integration Discovery - TidalFin / Redwood
summary: Discovery focused on integration patterns for Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Customer cares about LangChain/LlamaIndex SDK support, proxy/gateway topology, per-route rate limits, and observability hooks to tie into internal dashboards. Security team pre-qualified SOC2/KMS but asked about private VPC and audit logs. Next step: run a short benchmark and share security pack + sample LangChain integration snippets.
action_items: Samira: Share pricing sheet and dedicated capacity options by 2026-11-02
Derek: Provide LangChain + LlamaIndex example repo and a short demo notebook by 2026-11-04
Evan: Send list of security questions (SAML/KMS/audit retention) to Redwood by 2026-11-01
next_steps: Deliver security pack (SOC2, ISO docs, KMS integration guide)
Provision trial hosted tokens and run micro-benchmarks with customer's 2 sample prompts
Schedule a follow-up technical POC call (SE-led) next week
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-30 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Derek Wong (Redwood SE), Maya Iyer (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (TidalFin CTO), Clara Gomez (Platform Eng), Evan Park (Security), Jules Martin (Product)

Auto-generated Summary (may be rough): Integration discovery re: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, SDK support, gateway topology, rate limits, observability.

00:00:05 Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time—uh quick intros, i'm Samira, AE at Redwood.
00:00:12 Rajiv: Hey Samira, Rajiv here, CTO at TidalFin. we'll grab context quickly.
00:00:18 Clara: Clara, platform eng, i'm the one who will actually wire this in.
00:00:22 Derek: Derek, SE, i'll cover the integration bits and non-functional.
00:00:30 Evan: Evan, security lead, i'll ask the hard questions.
00:00:35 Samira: Nice — agenda is integration patterns, SDKs (LangChain/LlamaIndex), gateway/proxy, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Anything to add?
00:00:45 Rajiv: No, that's perfect. We want to understand hosted first, then dedicated and private tradeoffs.
00:01:10 Derek: Quick high level: Hosted API is fastest to try — REST/SDK, streaming, but if you need VPC or strict data residency, Dedicated or Private are the paths. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput; Private gives you a customer-managed control plane, on-prem if needed.
00:02:00 Clara: For our use case — we have PCI-adjacent workloads, not storing card data, but want strict audit logs and KMS control. Can you do customer-managed KMS?
00:02:12 Derek: Yes, we integrate with external KMS/HSM for Private deployments; Dedicated can also support customer KMS via our key-management integration depending on contract. For Hosted, we have managed keys but can support BYOK in some enterprise engagements — need legal/sales to align.
00:02:45 Evan: Audit logs — retention windows, can we ship to our SIEM?
00:02:52 Maya: We expose audit and access logs via the console and streaming hooks — can push to S3, or send logs via syslog/forwarder. Also we provide tracing hooks (OpenTelemetry) to pipe events into customer's observability stack.
00:03:20 Rajiv: Good. About SDKs — we use LangChain heavily and LlamaIndex in experiments. How first-class are your adapters?
00:03:30 Derek: We maintain community examples and a maintained SDK in Python and Node. LangChain support is present via a Redwood LLM wrapper; LlamaIndex connectors are covered in our examples repo. We'll share a repo and a small notebook. The wrapper supports streaming, function-calling-ish patterns, and a consistent rate-limit header.
00:03:58 Clara: Any rate limiting per-route? We want throttles on the embeddings route vs chat generation, different quotas for internal vs external traffic.
00:04:10 Derek: Yes, our routing layer supports per-route and per-api-key quotas. You can define policies: token-based quotas, request/sec, and burst windows. For Dedicated/Private you get more control and can implement network-side egress rules too.
00:04:40 Jules: And proxying — we typically run a gateway in front of all vendor APIs. Does Redwood support IP allow-listing and proxy-friendly headers?
00:04:50 Maya: We support static egress IPs for Dedicated and Private, and allow-listing for Hosted via enterprise configuration. We also support header passthrough for trace ids (x-request-id, traceparent) and can accept forwarded client-ip.
00:05:20 Evan: TLS and mutual TLS? We need mTLS for internal agent calls in some zones.
00:05:26 Derek: Private deployment can be mTLS-enabled; Dedicated supports mTLS for customer-facing gateways with config. Hosted - we offer standard TLS; for mTLS we generally recommend Private.
00:05:50 Rajiv: Latency is a concern — we do synchronous chat helpers in our checkout flow, need sub-200ms p95 for small prompts. Any guidance on batching vs latency?
00:06:05 Derek: It's a classic tradeoff — batching reduces cost but adds latency. Our runtime has continuous batching and prefix caching; you can tune batching windows per route. For sub-200ms p95, you'd run lower batch windows or dedicated capacity sized for peak. Also quantized model variants can reduce latency.
00:06:30 Clara: Do you expose real-time metrics per-token cost and latency per model?
00:06:35 Maya: Console shows token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency, and per-model histograms. Also a metrics API to pull into Grafana via Prometheus exporter.
00:06:48 Rajiv: Good — we need those hooks. On the LangChain side, how do you handle streaming in the SDK? We stream token deltas back?
00:06:58 Derek: Yes, SDK supports streaming with incremental tokens and chunked JSON lines; LangChain agents can consume via our callback handler. We'll send sample LLMChain examples.
00:07:20 Jules: For LlamaIndex, we want connector support to hit embeddings endpoint, and index building off a private bucket. Anything special?
00:07:30 Derek: Embeddings are standard REST endpoints; you can push vectors to your vector DB. For private buckets, if using Private deployment, the data never leaves your VPC. For Hosted, you can use customer-managed S3 with VPC endpoints in enterprise setups.
00:07:55 Evan: SOC2 and ISO? We do require vendor SOC2 Type II.
00:08:00 Samira: Redwood is SOC2 Type II, and we have ISO 27001 documentation — we'll share the security pack after the call.
00:08:10 Evan: Encryption at rest — full-disk? customer keys?
00:08:15 Maya: Rest is encrypted; Private/Dedicated support BYOK. We'll include the KMS integration guide.
00:08:35 Rajiv: If we go Dedicated, what's the SLA?
00:08:40 Samira: Dedicated has an SLA for uptime and latency targets, plus reserved capacity and burst options. We'll send the SLA draft.
00:09:05 Clara: For onboarding, how fast can we spin up a Dedicated pool for a pilot?
00:09:12 Derek: Pilot Dedicated can be provisioned in days depending on region and GPU availability; for a quick POC we recommend using Hosted trial tokens while we provision Dedicated.
00:09:30 Rajiv: Network topology — we run a gateway in GCP us-east1. If you host in multiple regions, is there smart routing?
00:09:40 Maya: Yes, requests can be routed by region, latency, or cost policies. You can pin routes to region with fallbacks.
00:10:05 Jules: Observability — we want traces to include prompt hashes and model version. Is that supported?
00:10:15 Derek: We attach model id, model version, prompt hash, and token counts in the trace metadata; you can redact prompt text if needed.
00:10:40 Evan: Retention of prompts in logs — retention policy? We need 90 days for audit but not store PII.
00:10:50 Maya: You can configure retention windows and enable prompt redaction. Private gives you full control over storage.
00:11:22 Rajiv: Pricing — how granular is pricing? token-based? token + compute?
00:11:30 Samira: Hosted pricing is per-token and per-embedding unit; Dedicated is reserved capacity (monthly) plus usage overage; Private is licensing + infra. We'll share the pricing sheet.
00:12:05 Clara: For rate limits, can we set different quotas per team or per api key?
00:12:12 Derek: Yes, per-api-key quotas and per-route policies. You can also federate with your auth layer.
00:12:30 Rajiv: Any concerns integrating with our gateway — we run Kong + some Envoy sidecars.
00:12:38 Maya: We documented gateway patterns; Envoy/Kong proxies are supported. We usually recommend using a short-lived credential exchange and token rotation.
00:13:05 Rajiv: Cool. Can we run a micro-benchmark on Hosted then move to Dedicated if latency/cost require it?
00:13:13 Samira: That's the typical path. We'll provision trial tokens and a test dataset; Derek will help run a 2-3 prompt micro-benchmark.
00:13:30 Jules: About LlamaIndex — is there an official connector or do we need to adapt?
00:13:36 Derek: We have a maintained example connector and an adapter pattern; we'll send the repo. Some minor glue code usually required.
00:13:55 Clara: How do we handle model rollouts? We want canary to 10% then 100% if no regressions.
00:14:03 Maya: Console supports rollouts and canary traffic split by percentage, with automatic fallback to previous model on quality regressions. You can tie regressions to prompt test sets.
00:14:20 Rajiv: Nice. SLA and fallback — do you keep older model weights available?
00:14:26 Derek: Yes, you can pin model versions; runtime supports multiple coexisting variants.
00:15:00 Evan: Legal / data residency — can we have EU-only processing?
00:15:06 Samira: Yes, region pinning is supported for Hosted enterprise customers; Private naturally gives you full control.
00:15:30 Clara: Are there SDK differences between Hosted and Dedicated?
00:15:35 Derek: SDK calls are identical; differences are in credentials and endpoint URLs. For Private, you'd point the SDK to your control plane endpoint.
00:15:55 Rajiv: Fine. Any prebuilt observability connectors (Datadog, NewRelic)?
00:16:02 Maya: We have native Datadog metrics export, a Prometheus exporter for Grafana, and a few examples for NewRelic.
00:16:20 Jules: What about function/tool calling? We have tooling that expects structured JSON replies.
00:16:28 Derek: We support structured output and function calling patterns; SDK can surface structured outputs and validators.
00:16:45 Rajiv: For the micro-benchmark, we'll send 2 prompts: a short chat prompt (checkout helper) and an embeddings workload. Can you capture token-level timing?
00:16:55 Derek: Yes, our metrics capture token latency and end-to-end p95. We'll run both and return a perf spreadsheet.
00:17:15 Evan: For security review, i'll send a list of 30 detailed items — can you route to your security contact?
00:17:23 Samira: Absolutely — we'll loop in security and SRE.
00:17:40 Clara: Any gotchas with LlamaIndex streaming where tokenization differs?
00:17:47 Derek: Occasionally tokenizer differences across model variants cause length differences; we recommend normalizing tokenization on the client or using our SDK's token counter.
00:18:10 Rajiv: Great. Billing — we need consolidated invoices and per-team chargeback reporting.
00:18:18 Samira: We support consolidated billing and per-route cost attribution in the console.
00:18:40 Jules: Questions from product — do you support plug-in like external retrievals?
00:18:47 Derek: Retrieval augmented generation is common; you can set up retrieval hooks and pass retrieved docs as context.
00:19:05 Rajiv: Let's recap — we want: security pack, pricing, LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, micro-benchmark on Hosted, follow-up SE POC.
00:19:15 Samira: Correct. Derek, you'll own the LangChain repo and micro-bench?
00:19:21 Derek: Yep. I'll also run the perf tests with Clara's sample prompts.
00:19:30 Evan: Timeline — we need security answers within a week ideally.
00:19:36 Samira: We'll aim to send the security pack and the pricing by Monday.
00:19:45 Rajiv: Great. Any final questions?
00:19:50 Jules: None from product.
00:19:53 Clara: Nope.
00:19:55 Evan: All good.
00:20:00 Samira: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the items discussed.

notes: Customer prefers Hosted pilot -> Dedicated if performance needed. Security team requires SOC2 + KMS + audit logging. SE to run micro-benchmarks and provide LangChain examples.
